ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all shareholders, directors, proxy-holders, and UBOs against the UN Security Council consolidated list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, SEPBLAC and BOE national designations, and, for USD-corridor transactions, the OFAC SDN list. PEP determination follows Art. 14 Ley 10/2010 with enhanced due diligence and senior-management approval for high-risk PEPs; negative screening results must be evidenced in the AML file and archived for 10 years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) – www.rmc.es; electronic filing through the CIRCE portal – www.circe.es
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name may be in Spanish or any official language of the European Union; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters and accompanied by an official Spanish translation where required; the chosen name must be unique, truthful, and not mislead as to the corporate form (SL suffix mandatory in the deed).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The RMC certificate covers up to five proposals in order of preference and reserves the first available name for the applicant; reserve term is 3 months from issuance, renewable once for a further 3 months before expiry if the deed is not yet executed. Upon rejection the applicant may: (i) immediately re-file a new certificate request naming five alternative denominations without prejudice; (ii) within one month of an adverse final ruling, present a written re-consideration (recurso de alzada) to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública attaching evidence of prior use or trademark protection; (iii) escalate to the administrative courts (jurisdicción contencioso-administrativa) under Ley 39/2015 if the Registry does not cure the grounds within the statutory term.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for this low-risk MarTech/SaaS industry at formation: the registered address must be fixed in Spanish territory and able to receive official notifications (Art. 9 LSC). A purely virtual mailbox satisfies registry requirements but should be upgraded to a serviced office or co-working address to avoid tax-domicile re-characterization under Art. 8 Ley del Impuesto sobre Sociedades when the entity claims Spanish-resident benefits.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: approximately 15% annual probability for a no-inventory, low-risk digital analytics entity; 30–35% if the registered office is virtual-only with no personnel or upon VAT refund algorithm triggers; up to 50% if R&D tax credits or digital-nomad benefits are claimed in the first fiscal year.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), particularly Articles 19-30, 32, 62, 63, 78-82, 210-212, and 214-216; Law 14/2013 and Law 18/2022 apply to electronic formation and the minimum capital regime.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent Registro Mercantil Provincial for the company's registered office, coordinated nationally by the Registro Mercantil Central.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución), followed by registration with the competent Provincial Commercial Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The minimum share capital of a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 1, fully assumed and paid at incorporation. No statutory escrow account is required. Cash contributions may be paid into a company account before execution, but the founders may generally dispense with producing a bank certificate and assume responsibility for the existence and value of the contribution. Until equity reaches EUR 3,000, statutory reserve and creditor-protection rules apply under Article 4 of the Companies Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accept and record the subscription and full payment of its issued share capital as stated in the deed of incorporation and articles of association. RESOLVED, that the registered office be adopted at the address recorded in the deed and entered in the Commercial Registry. RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed sole director, or, where applicable, that the directors named in the deed be appointed to their respective offices, each accepting the duties and legal obligations of office. RESOLVED, that the appointed officer(s) be authorized to complete all tax, registry, banking, licensing, and operational formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central, online name-certificate service or authorized filing channel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to five proposed names and identify the intended company form as Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada. Obtain the negative name certificate and preserve its electronic verification code. The certificate is generally valid for three months for execution of the deed and six months for reservation purposes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is rejected, submit an alternative name or correct the proposed wording and refile. If the certificate expires, obtain a renewed certificate before signing the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and the selected Spanish notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a Spanish tax identification number for each foreign shareholder, director, and other required non-resident person through the AEAT or an authorized representative. Foreign corporate shareholders must provide legalized or apostilled constitutional documents, current registry evidence, tax identification, and a certified Spanish translation where required.
required_dossiers: Corporate shareholder certificate of incorporation and good standing
Apostille or legalization and sworn Spanish translation, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to AEAT or notarial requests with corrected identity, beneficial-ownership, legalization, or translation documents. Replace defective powers of attorney and resubmit the application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public (Notario) selected by the founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Provide the negative name certificate, articles of association, registered-office evidence, shareholder and director details, beneficial-owner information, capital allocation, management structure, and business purpose. Sign the escritura pública de constitución before the notary, either personally or through a notarized power of attorney. State that the capital is fully assumed and paid.
required_dossiers: Registered-office title, lease, or use authorization
Capital contribution statement or bank certificate if used
Foreign-language documents with required apostille and sworn translation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct deed observations before signature. If the notary refuses execution, obtain written reasons, cure the defect, and reschedule execution or challenge the refusal through the applicable notarial review procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Provisional Tax Identification and File Incorporation Tax Forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), through Modelo 036 and applicable electronic filing channels
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Modelo 036 to request the company's provisional NIF and register the principal business activity and tax address. Submit the notarized deed or its authorized electronic copy and identify the beneficial owner and directors. File the applicable transfer and stamp duty declaration; incorporation is generally exempt, but the filing requirement must be verified with the relevant autonomous community.
required_dossiers: Transfer and stamp duty declaration, where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct rejected Modelo 036 data, tax-address evidence, activity codes, or identification records and resubmit electronically. Obtain a replacement provisional NIF document if the initial record contains an error.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Company with the Provincial Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial for the registered office, generally through the executing notary's electronic filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request the notary to transmit the deed electronically or file the authorized copy directly with the Provincial Commercial Registry. Pay the registry and BORME publication charges, which are variable and are not a single fixed state incorporation fee. Monitor the registry entry and obtain the registration certificate and updated registry extract.
required_dossiers: Authorized electronic or paper copy of the incorporation deed
Proof of payment of registry and publication charges
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a qualification notice, cure the stated defect within the applicable period by filing an amended deed, corrected document, or supplemental evidence. A negative qualification may be appealed to the Directorate-General for Legal Certainty and Public Faith or challenged before the courts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Post-Registration Tax and Governance Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AEAT, Registro Mercantil Provincial, Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social, and the relevant autonomous-community or municipal authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the definitive NIF through Modelo 036, confirm the registered activity and tax obligations, legalize accounting and corporate books electronically through the Commercial Registry, and record the first governance resolutions. If employees or directors subject to social-security registration are engaged, complete the applicable TGSS registrations before commencement.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registry certificate or updated extract
Employment or director social-security documentation, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct tax, social-security, book-legalization, or beneficial-owner filing errors through the relevant electronic portal. Pay assessed surcharges or penalties where applicable and request administrative review if the assessment is factually or legally incorrect.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No sector-specific industrial licensing board is ordinarily required for a software, SEO analytics, data-crawler, or SaaS business. The competent premises authority is the relevant Ayuntamiento, and industrial or energy matters, if triggered, are handled by the corresponding autonomous-community industry department.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No specific manufacturing or industrial operating permit for the stated SaaS activity. A municipal activity declaration (declaración responsable de actividad) or operating licence may be required for physical premises, depending on the municipality and premises characteristics.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: The environmental authority of the relevant autonomous community; the national framework is administered by the Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico where state competence applies.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt from project-level EIA for ordinary office-based software and SaaS operations. EIA screening or a full EIA may arise only from a separately regulated construction, infrastructure, energy, industrial, or materially polluting project.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No routine industrial wastewater, VOC, or process-emission thresholds apply to ordinary office-based operations. Any discharge to public sewers, emissions, hazardous waste, batteries, electronic waste, or backup-power systems must comply with the applicable autonomous-community, municipal, water-authority, and waste-management permits and their site-specific limits under Spanish environmental legislation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For ordinary offices, obtain any required municipal activity declaration and comply with the Spanish Occupational Risk Prevention Act, workplace safety rules, accessibility requirements, and the applicable fire-protection regulations. Fire-safety certification, emergency planning, evacuation measures, electrical inspections, structural load verification, and occupational clearances become mandatory where required by the premises classification, building use, occupancy, equipment, or local authority.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); official e-office portal: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign shareholders and directors must first obtain a Spanish NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero). The Spanish SL is incorporated before a Notary, with the incorporation deed filed in the Mercantile Registry. Following registration, the company applies to AEAT for its definitive NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) using Form 036/037. The NIF serves as both the corporate tax reference and the VAT identification number; for intra-EU VAT purposes the identifier is the NIF prefixed with 'ES'.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists. A Spanish SL is statutorily a corporation subject to the corporate income tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) at the general rate of 25%, unless a reduced 15% rate applies for newly created entities under Article 29.1 of the Spanish Corporate Income Tax Law during the first two years of profitable activity. Available statutory elections include the tax consolidation regime for groups under Article 42 et seq. of the Corporate Income Tax Law, deductions for R&D and technology activities, the patent box regime, and transfer-pricing documentation thresholds. Hybrid mismatch rules have been implemented under ATAD.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA – Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold: any person performing taxable economic activities in Spanish territory must register for IVA from the first transaction. Non-resident suppliers become liable to register from their first taxable supply in Spain or when distance sales of goods to Spanish consumers exceed EUR 10,000 per calendar year under EU distance-selling rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taxpayers with annual turnover exceeding EUR 6,000,000 must file SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) real-time invoice data with AEAT within 4 working days of issuance or recording. All enterprises are subject to the Anti-Fraud Law (Veri*factu) over billing software integrity, unalterability, and AEAT accessibility. B2B electronic invoicing is mandatory under Law 18/2022 and the 'Crea y Crece' framework; invoices must be supplied electronically using compatible formats (Facturae XML for public-sector invoices). Digital certificates and AEAT web services or FTP are used for submissions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (exemption with deduction) applies to actual exports of goods, meaning goods are physically dispatched or transported from Spain and the European Union to a non-EU territory by the seller or on its behalf. The exemption also covers services directly related to export goods, international transport services, and certain B2B services supplied to non-EU customers where the place of supply is deemed to be outside Spain and therefore outside the scope of Spanish VAT. The supplier must hold evidence that goods have left EU territory and must fulfill the export reporting requirements in the VAT return and the customs export summary declaration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Single Administrative Document (DUA) / Electronic Export Declaration (DAE)
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR transport document
Commercial invoice referencing the export declaration and identifying buyer and destination
Proof of exit from EU customs territory or confirmation of customs clearance
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement evidencing receipt of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT scrutinizes export exemption claims through documentary checks and cross-referencing with customs data. Failure to substantiate the physical export or receipt of payment within the contractual timeframe can lead to the retroactive clawback of zero-rated VAT, the recharacterisation of the supply as taxable, and the assessment of the outstanding IVA plus late-payment interest. Fraudulent or consciously negligent claims may attract tax penalties up to 150% of the tax amount, loss of deduction rights, and, in criminal cases involving tax amounts exceeding EUR 120,000, prosecution under Article 305 of the Spanish Criminal Code.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting within the Eurosystem; foreign-investment and certain external-transaction reporting functions are administered under the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business, including the Directorate-General for Trade and Investments. Anti-money-laundering supervision and suspicious-transaction reporting are handled through SEPBLAC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain uses the euro, which is fully convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions. There is no general exchange control, mandatory repatriation rule, or restriction on converting euro receipts into foreign currency. Cross-border dividends, interest, royalties, service fees, loan repayments, and capital returns may generally be remitted subject to corporate approvals, distributable-profit rules, withholding-tax analysis, transfer-pricing requirements, beneficial-owner verification, sanctions screening, and bank evidence requirements. EU sanctions, anti-money-laundering rules, foreign-investment screening, tax anti-abuse rules, and restrictions involving sanctioned persons or jurisdictions remain applicable. A Spanish SL must maintain sufficient accounting and tax support for related-party funding, deductible interest, royalties, management charges, and distributions. Non-resident shareholders may face Spanish withholding tax unless a domestic exemption, EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief, or applicable tax treaty applies and the relevant beneficial-ownership and substance conditions are satisfied.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to the central bank, convert them into euros, or repatriate them within a prescribed period. Export proceeds may remain in euro or foreign-currency accounts, including accounts outside Spain, subject to accounting, tax, sanctions, customs, and anti-money-laundering obligations. There is no general mandatory conversion ratio. The company must retain invoices, customs declarations, transport evidence, customer contracts, bank statements, and VAT documentation supporting the transaction. External-payment and foreign-investment statistical declarations may apply under Spanish rules when applicable, generally through the authorized financial institution or the prescribed electronic filing system; the bank may request transaction-purpose information and supporting documents before execution. Export VAT zero-rating or exemption requires the applicable customs or transport evidence, and intra-EU supplies require valid VAT identification and associated reporting.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for payment collection, card expenditure, SEPA transfers, and multi-currency treasury where the provider is an EU-authorized electronic-money institution or payment institution passported into Spain. An offshore provider without EU authorization, passporting, or an appropriately authorized local establishment cannot lawfully provide regulated payment or e-money services to the Spanish SL merely through a foreign website. EMI funds are safeguarded and are not equivalent to insured bank deposits. Availability of local Spanish IBANs, beneficiary-name matching, SEPA Instant access, SWIFT capability, client-money segregation, safeguarding disclosures, account statements, and tax-audit support must be verified. Stripe and Paddle may support collection and merchant settlement but do not replace a principal operating bank account, and their reserves, rolling holds, chargeback procedures, prohibited-business rules, and settlement-country restrictions must be incorporated into liquidity planning.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors are not universally required to appear physically in Spain. Remote onboarding may be available through video identification, qualified electronic identification, Spanish electronic certificates, notarized powers of attorney, and certified corporate documents. The bank may nevertheless require an in-person meeting for non-resident directors, complex ownership chains, unusual transaction profiles, high-risk jurisdictions, foreign-language documents, absence of Spanish operating substance, or unresolved beneficial-owner questions. Banks commonly require identification of directors, authorized signatories, ultimate beneficial owners, and controlling persons; Spanish tax identification numbers or foreign tax identifiers; notarized or legalized documents where applicable; proof of address; corporate registry evidence; and a clear explanation of the expected payment flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder or director with no Spanish tax identification number, incomplete identification, or inconsistent names across passports, corporate records, and bank forms.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current passport or national identity document; Spanish NIF/NIE where required; certified proof of residential address; notarized powers of attorney; corporate registry extracts; apostilled or legalized documents where required; certified translations; and a signed identity-matching schedule explaining name variations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership chain, nominee shareholder, trust arrangement, bearer-like control, or inability to identify the ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete ownership chart through every intermediate entity to each natural-person beneficial owner; registry extracts for all entities; shareholder registers; constitutional documents; declarations of beneficial ownership; board resolutions; trust or foundation documents where relevant; and evidence of control rights.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign inbound capital described only as 'investment' or 'loan' without a legally consistent instrument and commercial rationale.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription or shareholder-loan agreement; board and shareholder approvals; source-of-funds evidence; originating bank statements; capitalization table; transfer-pricing analysis for related-party debt; repayment and interest terms; applicable foreign-investment declarations; and a payment instruction identifying the precise legal purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected activity inconsistent with a newly incorporated SEO, content analytics, or MarTech SaaS company, including high-volume pass-through payments, cash activity, cryptocurrency flows, or unexplained third-party collections.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan; product demonstrations; website and terms of service; customer segmentation; signed customer contracts; invoices; Stripe and Paddle agreements; forecast transaction volumes and countries; payroll and supplier budgets; source-of-revenue schedule; and a written funds-flow map distinguishing customer receipts, refunds, taxes, payroll, suppliers, and shareholder funding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving sanctioned jurisdictions, politically exposed persons, high-risk countries, privacy-enhancing cryptocurrency services, or counterparties with adverse media.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty due-diligence file; sanctions-screening results; beneficial-owner verification; contract and invoice; end-use statement; shipping or service-delivery evidence; adverse-media resolution memorandum; compliance approval; and documented prohibition of transactions that cannot be cleared under EU, Spanish, UN, or applicable US sanctions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large or repeated transfers between the Spanish SL and related parties lacking arm's-length pricing or supporting services.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Intercompany agreements; transfer-pricing master and local-file support where applicable; service descriptions; time records; deliverables; comparable pricing; withholding-tax analysis; VAT analysis; board approvals; invoices; and evidence that the recipient performed the stated services.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of a virtual office, registered-office address, residential address, or Spanish company with no apparent local management or economic activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease or serviced-office agreement; employee or contractor records; director-residency and management explanation; customer and supplier contracts; Spanish tax registrations; accounting records; operational calendar; local service-provider agreements; and a written substance and governance memorandum.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent foreign-currency conversions, unexplained transfers to personal accounts, or payment flows that bypass the principal corporate account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury policy; approved bank-account matrix; dual-authorization controls; monthly bank reconciliations; foreign-exchange policy; board-approved intercompany payment procedures; payroll records; expense policy; and transaction-level invoices and approvals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete tax, accounting, or beneficial-ownership filings, including inconsistencies between bank information, Agencia Tributaria records, commercial registry data, and annual accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current tax registration certificates; filed corporate-tax and VAT returns where available; annual accounts; commercial-registry extract; beneficial-ownership information; accountant confirmation; reconciliation of registered activities and bank activity; and remediation evidence for any historical discrepancy.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route shareholder equity, share-premium funding, or shareholder loans from an account held in the verified name of the investor directly to the Spanish SL's account at an EU-regulated bank. Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro funding and SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA currencies or banks. The payment reference should identify the Spanish SL, investor, legal instrument, and purpose, such as 'share capital contribution', 'share premium contribution', or 'shareholder loan under agreement dated [date]'. Avoid third-party funding, cash deposits, unexplained payment intermediaries, and personal accounts. Before receipt, provide the bank with the subscription or loan agreement, corporate approvals, ownership chart, source-of-funds evidence, expected amount and currency, and beneficial-owner information. The bank should verify the originating account, sanctions status, source and purpose of funds, and whether any foreign-investment or statistical declaration is required. Convert currencies through the bank or an authorized EU investment-services or payment provider under documented treasury limits. Record the transaction in the general ledger, reconcile the bank credit, and retain the SWIFT or SEPA confirmation, exchange-rate evidence, and supporting corporate documentation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant for euro payments to EU suppliers where available. Use SWIFT MT103 for international supplier, contractor, tax, and service payments outside SEPA. For documentary trade, use an irrevocable documentary letter of credit subject to UCP 600, preferably confirmed where country or bank risk warrants, and require compliant commercial invoices, transport documents, insurance documents, packing lists, certificates of origin, and inspection documents. Use documentary collections under URC 522 where a lower-cost alternative is commercially acceptable. For service and SaaS payments, retain the contract, invoice, proof of performance, VAT treatment, withholding-tax assessment, and beneficiary verification. For exports, retain customs declarations, transport evidence, customer order, invoice, delivery evidence, and VAT support. Establish dual approval, beneficiary call-back verification, segregation of duties, sanctions screening, invoice-fraud controls, payment limits, and a documented exception process. MT103 is a payment message and does not itself prove trade compliance; the commercial and customs dossier must be retained separately.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward exchange contracts with an authorized bank or regulated investment firm, used to hedge documented forecast or contracted euro and foreign-currency exposures and supported by an approved treasury policy.

Non-deliverable forwards where the relevant currency is non-deliverable or local regulation prevents physical settlement; settlement should occur in the agreed convertible currency and be supported by the underlying exposure and counterparty documentation.

Currency swaps or cross-currency interest-rate swaps for documented recurring cash-flow or debt exposures, subject to counterparty credit limits, collateral terms, valuation controls, and applicable EU derivatives requirements.
Plain-vanilla foreign-exchange swaps for short-term liquidity management and settlement-date mismatches, subject to documented commercial purpose and authorized-counterparty controls.
Foreign-exchange options or collars where the company accepts premium, valuation, accounting, and suitability risks and the instrument is proportionate to the underlying exposure.

Hedging with an EU-authorized bank or investment firm must comply with applicable MiFID II conduct requirements, EMIR obligations where applicable, derivatives reporting and risk-mitigation rules, contractual netting and collateral documentation, and internal limits. Speculative trading, leveraged products without a documented exposure, and transactions with unregulated counterparties should be prohibited.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Deposit (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial (Commercial Registry of the province of the registered office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' ordinary meeting must approve the annual accounts within six months after the fiscal-year end; deposit with the Registro Mercantil within one month after approval; calendar-year SL by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Cierre registral: the company cannot register further corporate acts until the annual accounts are deposited; ICAC fines of EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000 for late or defective filing; no administrative strike-off is triggered solely by late deposit.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days after six months following the close of the tax period; calendar-year SL by 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharges (5%, 10%, or 20% depending on delay) plus monthly late-payment interest; AEAT may assess tax on an estimated basis and impose penalties; tax delinquency does not cause administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for an SL that satisfies at least two of the following for two consecutive years: total assets exceeding EUR 2,850,000; net turnover exceeding EUR 5,700,000; annual average of more than 50 employees. Audit is also required where consolidated accounts are prepared or where applicable law imposes audit for the entity's activities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad, Real Decreto 1514/2007); small entities may apply the PGC Pymes; EU IFRS applies to consolidated accounts when the group is required to use it, while individual SL statutory accounts use Spanish GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spain does not require a standalone annual UBO confirmation form. Each share transfer must be recorded in the Libro Registro de Socios and, for SL participations, formalized in an authentic notarial or equivalent document before inscription in the register. UBO data must be kept current for purposes of Law 10/2010 anti-money-laundering obligations and must be updated before notarial or registry acts whenever a change occurs.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Annual Accounts and Inventory Book (Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $450–$1,300 per year for registered-office services and professional corporate administrator/legal representation, depending on province and service provider.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $3,000–$10,000 for a small-to-mid-sized Spanish SL audit, depending on turnover, asset structure, and transaction complexity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general Spanish Corporate Income Tax rate. Newly incorporated entities may apply 15% during the first profitable tax period and the following tax period, subject to statutory eligibility and anti-abuse conditions. Qualifying newly created innovative start-ups may also apply 15%. Additional reduced rates may apply to qualifying microenterprises and other specifically regulated entities.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Spain operates a tax-credit and deduction system rather than a general tax holiday. Potential incentives include the 15% newly incorporated entity rate, research and development and technological innovation credits, audiovisual and qualifying investment credits, patent-box relief for qualifying net income from certain intellectual property, double-tax relief, employment-related incentives, and deductions subject to statutory caps and documentation. The 15% rate is unavailable where the company forms part of a pre-existing business activity or fails the statutory newly incorporated entity conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward period. Utilization is generally limited to 70% of the pre-utilization tax base, reduced to 50% for entities with prior-year net turnover of at least EUR 20 million and below EUR 60 million, and 25% for entities with prior-year net turnover of at least EUR 60 million, subject in all cases to the statutory minimum offset of EUR 1 million and applicable group and restructuring rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Spanish Corporate Income Tax and Non-Resident Income Tax return for permanent establishments, filed electronically through the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) electronic headquarters. Modelo 202 is used for mandatory advance Corporate Income Tax payments where applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Modelo 200: annual. Modelo 202: normally three advance-payment periods per year, in April, October and December.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Modelo 200 is due within the 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year company ending on 31 December, the normal filing and payment window is 1 to 25 July of the following year, subject to the applicable electronic-filing calendar. Modelo 202 is generally due from 1 to 20 April, 1 to 20 October and 1 to 20 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SL legal name, Spanish tax identification number, tax period dates, registered address, legal form, activity classification and filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder does not file Modelo 200 merely because it owns shares. The Spanish SL files as a Spanish resident taxpayer. A non-resident permanent establishment uses the applicable Modelo 200 permanent-establishment classification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the profit or loss under Spanish statutory or accepted accounting records before Corporate Income Tax and reconcile it to the taxable base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only income and expenses attributable to the Spanish resident company. Foreign shareholder accounting is not substituted for the Spanish SL's books.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report permanent and temporary tax adjustments, including non-deductible expenses, provisions, depreciation differences, impairment, exempt income, related-party adjustments and other statutory corrections.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Spanish deductibility rules. Payments to foreign related parties must be supported by arm's-length evidence, business purpose, beneficial ownership analysis and withholding-tax review.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report available tax losses, losses utilized in the period and remaining losses, applying the turnover-based utilization limitations and the EUR 1 million minimum threshold.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of a foreign shareholder or foreign group company cannot be used by the Spanish SL unless a specific Spanish tax consolidation, restructuring or other statutory rule applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the taxable base after adjustments and loss utilization, then apply the legally applicable rate, including any qualifying 15% or other reduced rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not apply a reduced rate solely because the shareholder is non-resident or because the business is digital. Eligibility must be demonstrated from Spanish statutory conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim qualifying R&D, technological innovation, investment, employment, double-taxation and other credits with supporting schedules and documentary evidence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign taxes may qualify for Spanish double-tax relief only within statutory limits and with evidence of payment and foreign-source income. Treaty relief is not itself a Corporate Income Tax credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Payments on account and withholding credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset Modelo 202 payments, Spanish withholding taxes and other authorized prepayments against final Corporate Income Tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Spanish withholding on payments received by the SL is creditable only where properly documented and legally attributable to the SL.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the final amount payable or refundable, select direct debit or other approved payment method, and retain the electronic filing receipt.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A refund claim should be supported by reconciliations, bank details, accounting records and evidence explaining any material cross-border transactions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Related-party transaction and tax information schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose applicable related-party transactions, tax adjustments, participation information, tax group information and other mandatory annexes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose dealings with non-resident parent, subsidiaries, affiliates, directors, financing entities, IP owners and service companies where the statutory schedules apply.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without tax due may attract a fixed penalty generally ranging from EUR 200 to EUR 250, reducible in certain circumstances. Where tax is unpaid, voluntary late filing before assessment generally produces a surcharge of 1% for each complete month of delay during the first 12 months, without penalty, and 15% after 12 months plus late-payment interest. If the filing is not voluntary and the authorities assess the liability, penalties for incorrect or omitted tax may generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, depending on severity, with interest and possible criminal exposure. Modelo 202 non-payment may generate surcharges, interest and enforcement costs.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, advance Corporate Income Tax payment return filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly payment windows, normally three times annually.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Normally 1 to 20 April, 1 to 20 October and 1 to 20 December. Payment by direct debit normally requires an earlier statutory banking instruction deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the Spanish SL tax identification number, tax period, accounting period and applicable payment period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish SL's identification details, not those of the foreign shareholder.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the advance payment under either the prior-year tax-liability method or, where mandatory or elected, the current-period tax-base method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include current-period taxable items and related-party adjustments when the current-period method applies. Foreign group results are excluded unless legally attributable to the Spanish taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the statutory percentage and deduct eligible prior payments or credits to determine the amount payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not reduce the amount for foreign shareholder taxes or expected future dividends unless a specific Spanish rule permits the reduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Submit electronically and pay through an authorized bank channel or other AEAT-approved mechanism.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain payment confirmations and reconcile all Modelo 202 amounts to Modelo 200.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late voluntary payment generally triggers statutory surcharges and late-payment interest. Failure to make required advance payments may also result in interest, enforcement proceedings and a final-payment shortfall when Modelo 200 is filed.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish withholding tax is generally applicable to dividends paid by a Spanish SL to a non-resident. The domestic participation exemption for qualifying EU or European Economic Area corporate parent companies may eliminate withholding where the statutory conditions are satisfied, including qualifying legal form and subject-to-tax requirements, at least 10% direct or indirect participation, and the minimum holding-period requirement or undertaking. A treaty may reduce the rate, commonly to 0%, 5%, 10% or 15%, depending on the treaty and ownership conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a current tax residence certificate from the recipient's foreign tax authority, verify beneficial ownership and treaty eligibility, confirm limitation-on-benefits or anti-abuse requirements where relevant, and retain ownership, holding-period and subject-to-tax evidence. Apply the reduced or zero rate only where Spanish domestic law, the applicable double-tax treaty and administrative requirements permit it. If documentation is unavailable at payment, withhold at the domestic rate and pursue refund or regularization through the AEAT procedure. File the applicable withholding return, normally Modelo 216, and annual recipient information return, normally Modelo 296. Dividend exemption under the EU Parent-Subsidiary regime requires separate statutory verification and is not automatic.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: For payments by a Spanish resident company to non-residents, Spanish domestic withholding is generally 19% for interest and royalties paid to EU or EEA residents satisfying the relevant conditions and generally 24% for other non-residents, subject to statutory classifications and exemptions. The EU Interest and Royalties Directive may provide an exemption for qualifying associated EU companies, generally requiring qualifying legal forms, subject-to-tax status, minimum direct ownership and a minimum holding period. Tax treaties commonly reduce interest withholding to 0% or 5% to 15% and royalties to 5% to 10% or another treaty-specific rate. Treaty access requires residence certification, beneficial ownership, anti-abuse compliance and evidence that the payment is not recharacterized as a dividend, service fee or disguised distribution.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Spain generally exempts formal related-party documentation where the aggregate value of related-party transactions with the same person or entity does not exceed EUR 250,000 at arm's-length value during the tax period, subject to exclusions and special rules. Documentation requirements may apply by transaction category at lower thresholds, particularly for transactions involving real estate, intangible assets, tax jurisdictions listed under Spanish anti-abuse rules and certain business transfers. A Spanish entity forming part of a multinational group may require a Local File and Master File under the Spanish Corporate Income Tax regulations. Country-by-Country reporting generally applies to qualifying multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate a standalone Cayman-style Economic Substance Regulation regime for ordinary Spanish SLs. Substance is nevertheless relevant through the general anti-abuse rule, simulated-transaction doctrine, beneficial-ownership requirements, treaty anti-abuse standards, controlled foreign company rules, EU anti-hybrid rules, interest-limitation rules and the principal-purpose test in applicable treaties. The SL should maintain genuine Spanish management, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises or demonstrable business infrastructure, decision-making records, customer and supplier contracts, functional risk control, IP and data governance, and accounting evidence proportionate to its SEO analytics SaaS activity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Income Tax evasion and fraudulent tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional concealment of revenue, fabricated expenses, false invoices, undeclared payment accounts, intentional underreporting of taxable profit or fraudulent use of tax losses causing tax damage exceeding the criminal threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Ordinary tax fraud may constitute a criminal offense where the evaded tax exceeds EUR 120,000 for the relevant tax period and tax. Sanctions generally include imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and a fine of 1 to 6 times the amount defrauded, together with payment of the tax, interest and civil liability. Aggravated cases, including amounts exceeding EUR 600,000 or specified organized or fraudulent conduct, may attract imprisonment of 2 to 6 years and a fine of 2 to 6 times the amount defrauded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may incur criminal liability, civil restitution, fines, disqualification from public office or management, and subsidiary liability for tax debts where statutory requirements are met. Travel restrictions or other precautionary measures may be imposed by judicial authorities; imprisonment is possible in criminal cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False invoicing, sham services and transfer-pricing manipulation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging the Spanish SL for non-existent group services, inflating SaaS or SEO costs, routing profits through a foreign IP or marketing company without functions, or using unsupported management fees to shift Spanish profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustments may increase the taxable base and trigger late-payment interest and penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax depending on concealment, fraud and aggravating circumstances. False invoices may also constitute accounting or tax crimes where criminal thresholds and intent requirements are satisfied.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving fictitious or unsupported transactions may face civil liability to the company, tax derivation, criminal liability for fraud or accounting offenses, disqualification and personal fines. Corporate veil protection does not shield deliberate fraud or unlawful asset extraction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to withhold or remit non-resident tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, interest or service fees to foreign recipients without withholding, applying a treaty rate without a valid residence certificate, or failing to file Modelo 216 and Modelo 296.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Spanish SL may be assessed for the unwithheld tax, late-payment interest and withholding penalties. Penalties depend on the nature and severity of the omission and may generally reach 50% to 150% of the unpaid amount where a tax infringement is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face subsidiary tax liability or civil claims where they caused or tolerated the failure and statutory derivation conditions are satisfied. Deliberate concealment, falsification or repeated evasion may create criminal exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, treaty abuse and lack of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Spanish SL with nominee directors, no operational capacity, no genuine customer or supplier activity, circular payments, pass-through ownership, or an arrangement designed principally to obtain treaty or EU withholding relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AEAT may deny treaty or EU directive relief, recharacterize transactions, apply withholding and Corporate Income Tax adjustments, impose interest and penalties, and invoke Spain's general anti-abuse and simulated-transaction rules. Benefits may be denied even where formal documentation exists.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may face tax derivation, civil damages, disqualification and criminal exposure where sham conduct, money laundering or tax fraud is proven. The corporate form does not protect persons using the SL as an artificial conduit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining parallel books, deleting transaction logs, falsifying revenue recognition, manipulating customer analytics data, backdating contracts, or recording fictitious assets, liabilities or related-party balances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Consequences include tax reassessment, accounting and tax penalties, rejection of deductible costs, possible commercial-law sanctions and criminal accounting-document offenses where statutory elements are met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, finance officers and persons authorizing false records may incur personal criminal, civil and tax liability, including disqualification and restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify the ultimate beneficial owner, accepting anonymous or unexplained funds, processing suspicious payments through Stripe, Paddle or banking channels, ignoring sanctions indicators, or failing to retain customer due-diligence records where the company is subject to AML obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Spanish AML legislation, serious infringements may attract fines generally from EUR 60,000 to EUR 150,000 per infringement, while very serious infringements may attract fines from EUR 150,000 to EUR 5 million or up to 10% of annual turnover, subject to statutory limits and aggravating factors. Additional public reprimands, authorization restrictions and management disqualification may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible directors and officers may receive personal fines, temporary disqualification and other administrative sanctions. Knowing participation in laundering may constitute a criminal offense carrying imprisonment, fines and asset confiscation; precautionary travel restrictions may be ordered in judicial proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to maintain Spanish books, records and supporting evidence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Inability to produce invoices, contracts, payroll records, bank reconciliations, source-code and IP ownership evidence, user-revenue logs, intercompany agreements, or transfer-pricing analyses during an AEAT inspection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may reject deductions, estimate the tax base, impose record-keeping and obstruction penalties, assess unpaid tax and interest, and apply broader tax penalties where the missing evidence conceals taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil and tax liability if the record failure is deliberate, obstructive or part of fraudulent conduct. Routine negligence generally creates corporate rather than automatic personal liability, subject to statutory derivation rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Improper profit distribution and unlawful asset extraction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends without distributable profits, impairing legally protected capital or reserves, paying shareholder loans disguised as expenses, or transferring company assets to related parties below market value.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Distributions may be repayable, related-party payments may be recharacterized as dividends or remuneration, and tax, interest and penalties may apply. Spanish Companies Law remedies may include restitution, director liability and shareholder claims.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly liable for unlawful distributions, corporate losses and creditor damage where statutory duties are breached. Fraudulent extraction may additionally support insolvency, civil and criminal proceedings.
